subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design is correct and internally consistent. (1) CORRECTNESS: seed-first works because auto-release triggers on Self Test workflow_run (push to main), not on tag/release creation — verified in auto-release.yml lines 14-18 — so manually seeding v0.4.0 fires no workflow (KD2). After seed, highest-semver-ancestor selection yields v0.4.0 as base; the hardening PR merge then computes v0.4.0..HEAD = only fix/ci/docs commits = patch -> v0.4.1, avoiding the v1.0.0 overshoot. gh release create --target tags fixed code (KD1). The hardening loop correctly excludes the floating v0 tag (glob requires two dots) and sort -V | tail -1 picks highest; merge-base --is-ancestor in a condition is set -e safe. Idempotency guard (skip if NEW_TAG exists) closes the double-fire window. (2) SIMPLICITY: a materially simpler alternative exists (delete the 3 stranded tags), but it was explicitly rejected by the user (OOS1) in favor of history preservation; given that constraint, seed+harden is the minimal correct path — no simpler option meets 'don't delete' + 'highest semver points at fixed code' + 'recurrence guard'. (3) SPEC-LAW: no formal adv_spec specs exist; the executable invariants in self-test.yml (exact 'Sharperflow CI Gate', no-bypass, squash-only, strict-off) are untouched — design adds no workflow paths: filter and edits only auto-release.yml base selection + docs. No conflict. (4) ALTERNATIVES: deletion (rejected by user), Renovate allowedVersions/ignore pinning (rejected as DONT3 manual-pin-adjacent and doesn't fix root cause), and workflow_dispatch version input were considered implicitly; the chosen seed+harden is the only one satisfying all of AC1-AC6 simultaneously.

validation.notes: Two non-blocking cautions: (C-a) The hardened base-selection loop runs git tag --list inside the workflow with fetch-depth:0 (already set) — confirm in execution that actionlint accepts the multi-line for-loop and that the unquoted command substitution does not trip SC2086 in any shellcheck pass over the workflow's run: block (actionlint embeds shellcheck). (C-b) AC1 says release '>= v0.4.0' and is highest semver: after seeding v0.4.0 the very next hardened auto-release will cut v0.4.1, so the durable 'highest semver points at fixed code' invariant holds for both; just ensure the v0.4.0 seed and the v0.4.1 auto-cut both target fixed main, never 5afaf289. Both cautions are execution-phase verification items, not design defects.

subagent_reports.recommendation: VALIDATED. Evidence confirms the trigger model (no workflow on tag creation), gh release --target tagging, and Renovate highest-semver proposal behavior. Proceed to planning. wisdom.content: In GitHub Actions `run: |` blocks, heredocs (`<<EOF`) break because the terminator must be column-0 but YAML indents everything; `<<-EOF` only strips tabs, not the spaces YAML uses. Use a bash here-string (`done <<< "$VAR"`) instead — it runs the while-loop in the current shell (so loop-set variables persist) and has no indentation-sensitive terminator. For "latest maintained release," select the highest-semver tag that is an ANCESTOR of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` + `sort -V | tail -1`), not nearest-ancestor `git describe --abbrev=0`, which silently regresses when higher-semver tags strand on older commits.

**AC1** Given `main` has the fixed `setup-bun-node` composite, when the version-line jump is applied, then a release at `v0.4.0` or higher exists whose tag points at fixed `main` code (never the broken `v0.3.2` commit) and is the highest semver tag in the repo.
**AC2** Given the `v0.4.0` release exists, when Renovate next evaluates a consumer (PokeEdge and/or PokeEdge-Web), then it proposes the `v0.4.x` line — verified on at least one consumer.
**AC3** Given known consumers are SHA-pinned, when the jump is applied, then no consumer CI breaks and existing SHA pins still resolve.

**AC4** Given auto-release version selection is hardened, when a higher-semver tag exists off the nearest-ancestor path, then auto-release selects the highest semver as its base so stranding cannot recur (verified by logic review + actionlint/self-test).
**AC5** Given the change is verified, when checks run, then actionlint passes for `auto-release.yml` and the repo self-test / ruleset invariants still pass.
**AC6** Given the version-line policy changed, when maintainers read the docs, then the `v0.4.0` jump and highest-semver auto-release behavior are documented.

**C2** The new highest-semver tag must point at fixed `main` code, never the broken `v0.3.2` commit.
**C3** Do not delete or rewrite git history/commits.
**C4** Changes to `auto-release.yml` must pass actionlint and must not bypass required status checks.
**C5** Tag/release operations must be auditable and reversible-by-recreate (record affected SHAs/IDs).
**DONT1** Do not break SHA-pinned consumers.
**DONT2** Do not weaken or bypass `Sharperflow CI Gate`.
**DONT3** Do not hand-edit consumer pins as the primary retarget mechanism (let Renovate raise the corrected PR).
**DONT4** Do not create any tag/release pointing at the broken `setup-bun-node` commit.
**OOS1** Deleting or yanking the stranded `v0.3.0/v0.3.1/v0.3.2` releases or tags (jump-forward to `v0.4.0` chosen instead).

# Remove stranded v0.3.x tags

## Why

`sharperflow-security-gates` has a version-line regression. The auto-release workflow uses `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (nearest ancestor tag by history), so it keeps bumping the `v0.2.x` line forward (latest `v0.2.24`, fixed). But three higher-semver release tags — `v0.3.0` (2026-05-23), `v0.3.1` (2026-05-24), `v0.3.2` (2026-06-05) — are stranded on older commits that are now ancestors of the `v0.2.x` releases.

Renovate sorts by **semver**, sees `v0.3.2 > v0.2.24`, and keeps proposing the stranded `v0.3.2` to consumers. `v0.3.2` is both **stale** (60 commits behind `main`) and **broken**: its `setup-bun-node/action.yml` has an unquoted `default:` colon on line 12, so the composite fails to load and any consuming job fails at setup. This produced PokeEdge-Web PR #109 (now closed), whose `Sharperflow CI Gate` was red for exactly this reason.

Desired outcome: make the maintained, fixed `v0.2.x` line the highest semver so Renovate retargets consumers correctly, without breaking SHA-pinned consumers.

## What Changes

Subject to discovery:

- Delete the stranded GitHub releases and git tags `v0.3.0`, `v0.3.1`, `v0.3.2` from `Sharper-Flow/sharperflow-security-gates`.
- Verify no consumer relies on a `@v0.3.x` tag ref (all known consumers are SHA-pinned).
- Let Renovate retarget consumers (PokeEdge, PokeEdge-Web) to the maintained `v0.2.x` line.
- Optionally harden `auto-release.yml` version selection so higher-semver tags cannot strand again.
- Document the version-line policy.

## User Outcomes

- Renovate proposes the maintained, fixed `v0.2.x` line to all consumers, not the broken stranded `v0.3.2`.
- Consumers (PokeEdge, PokeEdge-Web) can take routine security-gate updates without red CI from a broken composite action.
- SHA-pinned consumers keep working through the cleanup (no orphaned commits).
- Maintainers have a documented, monotonic version line and an auto-release that cannot re-strand tags.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Removal of stranded `v0.3.0`, `v0.3.1`, `v0.3.2` releases and tags in this repo.
- Pre-deletion consumer audit for `@v0.3.x` tag refs vs SHA pins.
- Verification that the maintained `v0.2.x` line is highest semver after cleanup and that Renovate retargets correctly.
- Optional hardening of `auto-release.yml` version-selection logic.
- Documentation of the version-line policy.

### Out of Scope

- Changing the security-gate scanning behavior delivered by `fixOsvRemediation`.
- Rewriting consumer pins by hand as the primary mechanism (prefer Renovate retarget; manual only if required).
- Broad redesign of the release pipeline beyond preventing tag stranding.
- Enabling Dependabot security updates (already decided against — Renovate owns updates).

### Must Not

- Must not delete or rewrite git history/commits (only tags/releases that are ancestors and safe to drop).
- Must not break SHA-pinned consumers.
- Must not introduce a tag that points at the broken `setup-bun-node` commit.
- Must not weaken or bypass `Sharperflow CI Gate`.

## Affected Code

- Git tags / GitHub releases `v0.3.0`, `v0.3.1`, `v0.3.2` (release state, not files).
- `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml` — `git describe --abbrev=0` nearest-ancestor selection is the latent cause (line ~41).
- Possibly `docs/ci-standard.md` / `README.md` — version-line policy documentation.
- Consumer repos `Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge` and `Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge-Web` — verification/retarget only.

## Related Repositories

- Primary: `Sharper-Flow/sharperflow-security-gates`.
- Consumers to verify/retarget: `Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge` (SHA-pinned `@cb39edc # v0.3.2`, python paths) and `Sharper-Flow/PokeEdge-Web` (SHA-pinned `@926408c # v0.2.1`).

## Constraints

- Preserve `Sharperflow CI Gate` contract and no-bypass branch protection.
- Tag deletions must be reversible-by-recreate (record SHAs before deletion).
- Renovate must end up proposing the maintained `v0.2.x` line.

## Impact

- Stops Renovate from chasing the broken stranded `v0.3.2`.
- Removes a latent CI-breakage trap for every JS/Bun consumer.
- Restores a monotonic, trustworthy version line.

## Context

- Auto-release uses conventional commits; latest release `v0.2.24` (2026-06-16), cut from current fixed `main`.
- `v0.3.2` tag SHA `5afaf289`; Renovate-resolved `v0.3.2` SHA `cb39edc` — both carry the broken `setup-bun-node/action.yml`; both are ancestors of `main`.
- PokeEdge-Web Dependabot alerts were enabled during this session; PR #109 was closed as superseded.

## Discovery Findings

### Discovery Checklist

| Step | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Skill Discovery | PASS | Considered ADV skills; no pending-review skill frontmatter; closest match adv-ci-release (release CI), partial. |
| Prior Research Extension | PASS | Extended fixOsvRemediation evidence + auto-release.yml read; added precise tag SHAs/release IDs and python-path validity. |
| Conflict & Related-Work Scan | PASS | No conflicting active change; related agenda items found; own-change NO_TASKS/NO_DELTAS expected. |
| Edge Case Investigation | PASS | Edge cases recorded for deletion, Renovate retarget, and reversibility. |
| Design Question Depth | PASS | Delete-vs-jump and hardening questions annotated with trust/blast/alternatives. |
| Draft Spec Delta Shapes | PASS | Draft rq-* deltas recorded. |
| Related Pattern Scan | PASS | Only v0.3.x are stranded-higher; no other stranded-higher tags. |
| LBP Check | PASS | Delete stranded tags is least-bad durable fix; internal change, no external tool needed. |

### Skills Considered

- `adv-ci-release`: partial — conventional-commit auto-release pattern is relevant background; not loaded as core (this is a cleanup/repair, not new release CI).
- `adv-cleanup` / `adv-triage`: tangential.
- No skill gap warranting creation; release-tag-hygiene is bounded and captured here.

### Extends

- `fixOsvRemediation` (archived this session): surfaced the broken `v0.3.2` `setup-bun-node` composite and PokeEdge/PokeEdge-Web pins.
  - New finding: precise tag SHAs and release IDs recorded (v0.3.0 `5c9d5cd` id 328401518; v0.3.1 `3ce9b06` id 328435780; v0.3.2 `5afaf289` id 335032903).
  - New finding: `setup-python-uv@cb39edc` is valid YAML, so PokeEdge's python path on v0.3.2 is NOT broken — only the bun-node composite is. PokeEdge is merely on a stale pin.
- `auto-release.yml` (read): uses `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` (nearest ancestor), which is why the line stays on v0.2.x while v0.3.x strand higher by semver.
- No `temp/*.md` or `docs/*-prep.md` research packs found.

### Conflict Scan

- `adv_change_list includeArchived:true`: no active change conflicts. `deepenSastDataflow` (draft) is unrelated.
- `adv_change_validate`: passed; `NO_TASKS`/`NO_DELTAS` expected pre-prep.
- `adv_agenda_list`: related items found and partially addressed this session:
  - `ag-aLQBEmtj` and `ag-dYpzMDK5`: PokeEdge-Web enable alerts + merge pin PR — alerts now enabled; PR #109 closed (not merged) because it targeted broken v0.3.2. These agenda items are superseded by this change's correct-retarget plan.
  - `ag-CaXs6Lkd`: verify pending gate-pin update doesn't change osv-scanner-action version — relevant when Renovate raises the corrected v0.2.x PR.

### Current State

- Tags `v0.3.0/v0.3.1/v0.3.2` are real, non-draft GitHub releases targeting `main`; all three are ancestors of `main`.
- `git tag --list 'v*.*.*' | sort -V | tail` → highest semver is `v0.3.2`; the maintained auto-release line tops out at `v0.2.24` (lower semver, newer code, fixed).
- Floating `v0` tag (`f365a1b`) is auto-rolled; consumers in scope pin specific SHAs, not `@v0`.
- `renovate.json` (this repo) has no `allowedVersions`; consumers extend the shared preset which groups github-actions without version restriction.
- Known consumers are SHA-pinned: PokeEdge `@cb39edc # v0.3.2` (python), PokeEdge-Web `@926408c # v0.2.1` (bun-node).
- Org code search for other consumers returned nothing (private repos not indexed).

### Edge Cases

1. Tag/release deletion mechanics
   - Deleting a GitHub *release* leaves the underlying git *tag*; both the release (by id) and the ref (`refs/tags/v0.3.x`) must be deleted for Renovate to stop seeing the tag.
   - A consumer (unknown) using `@v0.3.x` as a tag ref would break on deletion; mitigated because all known consumers are SHA-pinned and SHAs survive tag deletion.
2. Renovate retarget timing
   - Renovate may not re-evaluate immediately; consumers stay on their current working SHA pins until the next Renovate run raises a corrected PR.
   - If the shared preset or a consumer has cached/branch state referencing v0.3.x, a stale PR could linger; closing #109 already handled the one known case.
3. Reversibility
   - If deletion proves wrong, tags/releases can be recreated from the recorded SHAs (release notes regenerated), since commits remain reachable.

### Open Design Questions

1. Delete stranded `v0.3.x` vs jump the line to `v0.4.0`.
   - Trust model: user-facing version policy.
   - Blast radius: org-wide version perception + Renovate behavior; wrong choice leaves broken v0.3.2 installable or burns version numbers.
   - Alternatives: (a) delete v0.3.x releases+tags — cleanest, recommended; (b) cut `v0.4.0` from fixed main so the maintained line surpasses v0.3.x (leaves broken v0.3.2 installable); (c) Renovate `allowedVersions` pin on consumers — masks rather than fixes.
2. Harden `auto-release.yml` version selection now or as a follow-up.
   - Trust model: agent-resolvable design, but scope decision is joint.
   - Blast radius: future tag stranding recurrence.
   - Alternatives: switch `git describe --abbrev=0` to highest-semver selection (`git tag | sort -V | tail -1`) in this change; or defer to a follow-up change.
3. Retarget PokeEdge's stale `@cb39edc # v0.3.2` python pin in this change or via Renovate follow-up.
   - Trust model: joint.
   - Blast radius: PokeEdge CI currency.
   - Alternatives: let Renovate raise the corrected PR after cleanup (recommended, low-touch); or push a manual retarget PR now.

### Draft Spec Deltas

- `rq-strandedTagRemoval01` — Given stranded higher-semver tags `v0.3.0/v0.3.1/v0.3.2` exist, when the cleanup runs, then their GitHub releases and git tag refs are removed and the highest remaining semver tag is the maintained `v0.2.x` line.
- `rq-strandedTagSafety01` — Given known consumers are SHA-pinned, when the tags are deleted, then no consumer CI breaks and SHAs remain resolvable; tag SHAs are recorded for reversibility.
- `rq-renovateRetarget01` — Given the stranded tags are removed, when Renovate next runs on a consumer, then it proposes the maintained `v0.2.x` line (not a v0.3.x tag).
- `rq-autoReleaseHardening01` — Given the auto-release selects the next version, when a higher-semver tag exists off the maintained line, then version selection does not silently strand it (only if hardening is in scope).

### Related Pattern Scan

- Full tag list: `v0.0.0`, `v0.1.0`, `v0.2.0`–`v0.2.24`, `v0.3.0`–`v0.3.2`, plus floating `v0`.
- Only `v0.3.0/v0.3.1/v0.3.2` are stranded-higher than the maintained line. No other stranded-higher tags exist. `v0.0.0/v0.1.0` are lower and harmless.

### LBP Check

- Internal release-hygiene change; no external tool/library decision → External-Solution Check skipped (stated explicitly).
- Long-term best practice: a monotonic, single highest-semver line that matches newest code. Deleting the three stranded tags achieves that with minimal blast radius and full reversibility, and requires no workflow change. Hardening `auto-release.yml` to select highest semver is a sound recurrence guard but secondary.

### Discovery Opportunity Scout

- Scout: skipped — narrow internal release-tag cleanup with low opportunity surface; candidates already enumerated as design questions (delete vs jump, hardening, consumer retarget).

### Recommended Objectives

1. Remove the stranded `v0.3.0/v0.3.1/v0.3.2` releases and tags so the maintained `v0.2.x` line is the highest semver.
2. Preserve all SHA-pinned consumers and record tag SHAs for reversibility.
3. Ensure Renovate retargets consumers to the maintained line (verify post-cleanup).
4. Decide and apply the recurrence guard (auto-release hardening) now or record it as a tracked follow-up.
5. Document the version-line policy.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS

M1 HIGH Missing Information — the version-policy direction (delete v0.3.x vs jump to v0.4.0) is not yet decided.
  Evidence: "Decide intended version line going forward: continue `v0.2.x`, or deliberately jump to `v0.4.0` to surpass the stranded tags instead of deleting them."

# Design — removeStrandedV03XTags

## Architecture Overview

Two coordinated actions restore a monotonic, trustworthy version line without deleting the stranded `v0.3.x` tags:

1. **Deterministic forward jump to `v0.4.0`** — manually seed a `v0.4.0` release+tag pointing at current fixed `main` (`4606d05`, which has the quoted `setup-bun-node/action.yml`). This makes the highest semver tag point at working code and surpass the stranded broken `v0.3.2`.
2. **Auto-release recurrence guard** — change `auto-release.yml` base-version selection from nearest-ancestor (`git describe --abbrev=0`) to **highest-semver among ancestor tags**, plus an idempotency guard. After the jump, the maintained line (`v0.4.x`) is always the highest semver, so future auto-releases compute from it and cannot strand again.

The stranded `v0.3.0/v0.3.1/v0.3.2` releases are intentionally **left in place** (user decision: jump, not delete). They are no longer the highest semver, so Renovate stops proposing them.

## Key Decisions

### KD1 — Manual seed of `v0.4.0`, not conventional-commit auto-bump

Evidence: `git log v0.3.2..main` contains **0 `feat` and 0 breaking** commits. If the hardened auto-release computed a bump from base `v0.3.2`, it would produce a **patch → `v0.3.3`**, not the agreed `v0.4.0`. Relying on commit-message bumping cannot deterministically land `v0.4.0`.

Decision: cut `v0.4.0` explicitly via `gh release create v0.4.0 --target 4606d05…` (current fixed `main` HEAD). Deterministic, points at fixed code, honors the user's "jump to v0.4.0" intent exactly.

### KD2 — Seed BEFORE merging the hardening change (race-free ordering)

`auto-release.yml` triggers on `workflow_run` of **Self Test on main** (i.e. on push to `main`), **not** on tag/release creation. Therefore manually creating `v0.4.0` triggers **no** workflow.

Ordering:
1. Seed `v0.4.0` (+ roll floating `v0` → `v0.4.0`) from `main` HEAD. Highest semver is now `v0.4.0`. No workflow fires.
2. Land the `auto-release.yml` hardening + docs via the normal PR → `Sharperflow CI Gate` → merge flow.
3. On that merge, the **hardened** auto-release runs with base = highest semver = `v0.4.0`; range `v0.4.0..HEAD` = only the hardening commits (`fix`/`ci`/`docs`) → patch → `v0.4.1`, cut from fixed code. Monotonic and harmless.

This sidesteps any dependence on the 60 stranded historical commits and avoids an overshoot to `v1.0.0`.

### KD3 — Harden base selection to highest-semver ancestor + idempotency

Replace line ~41:
```bash
LAST_TAG=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match='v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*' 2>/dev/null || echo "v0.0.0")
```
with highest-semver selection restricted to **ancestor** tags (so a future stranded non-ancestor tag cannot hijack the base), falling back to highest overall, then `v0.0.0`:
```bash
# Prefer the highest-semver tag that is an ancestor of HEAD (the maintained line).
LAST_TAG=$(for t in $(git tag --list 'v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*'); do \
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$t" HEAD 2>/dev/null && echo "$t"; done | sort -V | tail -1)
[ -z "$LAST_TAG" ] && LAST_TAG="v0.0.0"
```
Add an idempotency guard before tagging: if the computed `NEW_TAG` already exists, skip cleanly instead of failing.

Rationale: highest-semver-ancestor is the correct "latest maintained release" and is immune to stranded higher tags on non-ancestor commits. `fetch-depth: 0` (already set) guarantees tags/history are present.

### KD4 — Leave `v0.3.x` installable; rely on Renovate retarget

Per user decision, `v0.3.x` releases/tags are not deleted. Because Renovate proposes the highest semver, consumers move to `v0.4.x`. PokeEdge's stale `@cb39edc # v0.3.2` python pin is retargeted by Renovate's next run (no manual PR). Known consumers are SHA-pinned, so nothing breaks during the transition.

## ADR Drafts

Candidate ADR (meets rubric: hard-to-reverse version-policy choice, surprising-without-context 0.3→0.4 jump while 0.2.x line continues, real tradeoff vs deleting tags). Draft `docs/adr/0001-version-line-jump-to-v0.4.0.md` is advisory and non-blocking; will be proposed during prep/execution if the repo adopts ADRs.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Worktree + branch** for the code change (`auto-release.yml` hardening + docs + optional ADR).
2. **Code**: harden base-version selection (KD3) + idempotency guard; document the version-line jump and highest-semver auto-release behavior in `docs/ci-standard.md` (and/or `README.md`).
3. **Verify locally**: actionlint on `auto-release.yml`; shell logic review; ruleset/self-test invariants unaffected.
4. **Release op (operator, audited)**: `gh release create v0.4.0 --target <fixed main sha>` and roll floating `v0` → `v0.4.0`. Record created tag/release IDs. Do this **before** merging the hardening PR (KD2), or immediately after with verification that highest semver is `v0.4.x` pointing at fixed code.
5. **Merge** the hardening PR via `Sharperflow CI Gate`.
6. **Verify**: highest semver tag = `v0.4.x`, points at fixed code (not the broken `v0.3.2` commit); Renovate proposes `v0.4.x` on at least one consumer (PokeEdge or PokeEdge-Web); actionlint + self-test pass.

## LBP Analysis

- Jump-forward + highest-semver-ancestor selection produces a **monotonic** version line that always matches newest code — the durable best practice for tag-driven Renovate consumers.
- Avoids deleting published releases (history-preserving, per user choice) while still removing the operational harm (Renovate no longer chases the stranded broken `v0.3.2`).
- The ancestor-restricted highest-semver base is strictly more correct than nearest-ancestor `git describe`, which silently regressed the line in the first place.
- Internal release-ops change; no external tool/library decision (External-Solution Check N/A).

## Affected Components

- `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml` — base-version selection (line ~41) + idempotency guard.
- `docs/ci-standard.md` / `README.md` — version-line policy + auto-release behavior docs.
- Optional `docs/adr/0001-version-line-jump-to-v0.4.0.md`.
- Release state: new `v0.4.0` release/tag; floating `v0` rolled to `v0.4.0` (operator action, not a repo file).
- Consumers (PokeEdge, PokeEdge-Web): verification/Renovate-retarget only; no direct edits.

## Design Leverage Scout

Scout: skipped — narrow release-ops + single-workflow change. Leverage points already enumerated as key decisions (manual seed vs auto-bump, race-free ordering, ancestor-restricted highest-semver selection, idempotency guard). Opportunity surface ≈ zero beyond these.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- **DDC1** The `v0.4.0` tag's commit must contain the quoted `setup-bun-node/action.yml` (fixed composite) — enforce by targeting current `main` HEAD, never a `v0.3.x` commit.
- **DDC2** Hardened base selection must restrict to ancestor tags so a stranded non-ancestor higher tag cannot become the bump base.
- **DDC3** Auto-release must be idempotent: never fail or duplicate when the computed tag already exists.
- **DDC4** All tag/release operations recorded (tag SHA, release id) for auditability and reversibility.

## Risks / Mitigations

- **Risk**: merge-triggered auto-release overshoots (e.g. `v1.0.0`) if it runs with base `v0.3.2` before the seed. **Mitigation**: KD2 ordering — seed `v0.4.0` first (no workflow fired), so the hardened run uses base `v0.4.0`.
- **Risk**: floating `v0` left at `v0.2.24` confuses `@v0` consumers. **Mitigation**: roll `v0` → `v0.4.0` during the seed.
- **Risk**: an unknown consumer pins `@v0.3.x` as a tag ref. **Mitigation**: tags are NOT deleted in this approach, so any such ref keeps resolving; Renovate still offers `v0.4.x` forward.
- **Risk**: broken `v0.3.2` remains installable. **Mitigation**: accepted by user (jump, not delete); no longer highest semver, so default Renovate path avoids it.
